contributions.statement: When a spec-driven pipeline emits requirement-to-artifact links at generation time, trust them only where the spec maps one requirement to one target element; check domain-concept links (requirement id to entity or DTO class) with a deterministic resolvability check or by review, because concept-level links reached only 0.53-0.72 F1 while 1:1 transition links were exact.
contributions.evidence: §4.6: requirement-to-transition links F1 1.00 for all three models over 18 transitions, but the requirement model was written one element per transition (§4.2). Requirement-to-concept micro-F1 0.53-0.72, and behaviour-link resolvability 0.73 for Sonnet 4.6. One AUV case study scored against an author-written reference, with no single-agent or post-hoc recovery comparator.
relative_to: 2606.24834 agent-produced requirement-to-code links need deterministic confirmation (code-location F1 about 0.2)

contributions.statement: Record a content hash of each requirement on every trace link and mark the linked downstream artifacts as suspect when the hash changes, so a requirement edit lists which generated files, tests and models need re-review.
contributions.evidence: §3.3 and §4.6: hash-versus-version comparison on Bifrost ExternalReferences; change-impact F1 1.00 over 180 injected behaviour-requirement changes per model, which holds by construction because the impact set is read off the same links.
relative_to: suspect-link flagging in requirements-management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama Connect, which the paper cites)

contributions.statement: When an LLM generates a structured artifact in a niche language (metamodel source, model-construction script), run the real parser or conformance checker and feed failures to a repair step; one-shot calls produced unparseable or non-conformant output in 50-100% of runs for two of three models.
contributions.evidence: Table 2, §4.5: DSML syntax-valid 0.50 -> 1.00 (DeepSeek-V4) and 0.00 -> 0.80 (Qwen3-max); conformant EOL 0/10 -> 10/10 (DeepSeek-V4). The baseline lacks both the agent roles and the gate, so the gain is not attributed to either alone.

contributions.statement: Adding checker and refactorer agent roles can lower the precision of generated design artifacts on some models, so score precision against a reference before adopting extra reviewer roles; Sonnet 4.6's metamodel class F1 fell from 0.92 to 0.86 because its check/refactor loop over-produced elements.
contributions.evidence: §4.5, Fig. 4: Sonnet 4.6 DSML class F1 0.92 -> 0.86 (Mann-Whitney p=1.1e-3); Qwen3-max concept F1 0.84 -> 0.80 (not significant). One model, one metamodel, one case study.
relative_to: 2609.38345 multi-agent gains must be checked against single-agent controls

reason: The only moderately supported finding, parse-and-repair beats one-shot generation, is established practice. The transferable traceability nuance, exact links for 1:1 spec elements versus 0.53-0.72 F1 for concept links, rests on one 18-transition case study with an author-written reference, so it stays a hypothesis.
